high.title: Key Banking Sector Limit to Be Relaxed Next Week: Lending Room for Real Estate, Infrastructure, and Business Production Could Expand by Trillions of VND
Contradictory Phenomenon Unfolding in the Stock Market — What Do Experts Say?
high.summary:
A notable divergence is emerging within Vietnam's equity market: while the VN-Index continues to hold elevated levels, the underlying breadth of the market remains weak. According to Luong Duy Phuoc, Head of Analysis at Kafi Securities, the index's resilience is being artificially supported by a narrow group of large-cap stocks — predominantly banking names and Vingroup — while the majority of listed equities are either consolidating or declining. This "green on the surface, red underneath" dynamic is a classic sign of deteriorating market internals.

Key concerns flagged by analysts include: (1) average daily liquidity in 2026 hovering around VND 26,000 billion/session, significantly below peak activity levels; (2) cautious money flows from domestic investors; and (3) continued net selling pressure from foreign investors.

high.title: State Bank of Vietnam Opens the "Valve" for Credit Growth
high.summary:
The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) has implemented a series of credit policy liberalization measures aimed at providing additional economic stimulus while maintaining risk control principles. Key regulatory changes include: (1) Circular 08 revising the Loan-to-Deposit Ratio (LDR) framework; (2) Circular 25 raising the maximum ratio of short-term capital used for medium- and long-term lending to 40%; and (3) an adjusted methodology for calculating credit growth that allows exclusion of certain specialized loan balances. Most notably, the SBV has agreed to exclude outstanding loans from 18 large-scale projects belonging to conglomerates including Sun Group, Vingroup, and Masterise from credit room calculations. Market analysts interpret this as effectively expanding available credit headroom for commercial banks without formally revising the headline credit growth target. **Key implications for investors:** This easing posture suggests SBV is prioritizing growth support over tightening. Broader credit availability could pressure deposit rates lower over time, weigh on bond yields at the short end, and support equity valuations in the banking sector. Monitor whether expanded credit supply translates into VND liquidity pressures or inflationary impulses in H2 2026.

high.title: "Releasing the Credit Valve": State Bank of Vietnam Signals Injection of VND 1.5 Quadrillion into Economy
high.summary: In a landmark and unprecedented policy shift, the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) has issued Official Dispatch No. 5386/NHNN-TD, allowing outstanding loans linked to 18 designated strategic projects to be **excluded from commercial banks' annual credit growth room (room tín dụng)**. This extraordinary carve-out applies specifically to three major conglomerates — Vingroup, Sun Group, and Masterise — with a combined capital demand of approximately **VND 752 trillion (~USD 28 billion)** over the 2026–2028 period. The earmarked funds are directed toward high-priority infrastructure: urban rail (Ben Thanh–Can Gio, Hanoi–Quang Ninh corridors), Phu Quoc International Airport expansion, Gia Binh Airport, and other large-scale infrastructure complexes.

medium.title: Green SM of Billionaire Pham Nhat Vuong Receives Over $1 Billion in Capital Injection YTD — Registered Capital Surpasses SHB and HDBank
medium.summary:
Green SM, the EV ride-hailing venture of Vietnam's wealthiest individual Pham Nhat Vuong, has raised its registered charter capital from VND 43,400 billion to VND 54,000 billion — its fourth capital increase in 2026 alone. Year-to-date, total capital injected exceeds the equivalent of USD 1 billion. The company is actively preparing for an international listing, with Reuters reporting in January 2026 that a Hong Kong IPO is being targeted for 2027, with a proposed valuation of approximately USD 20 billion.

This development is relevant for capital flow watchers: large-scale foreign capital mobilization into Vietnamese private enterprises — particularly ahead of an international IPO — can influence FX dynamics and investor appetite for Vietnamese assets broadly. If a Hong Kong listing materializes at the cited valuation, it would represent the largest-ever international capital markets event for a Vietnamese private company and could serve as a meaningful catalyst for both equity sentiment and USD/VND inflow dynamics.

medium.title: Bank Deposit Interest Rates as of June 27 — ACB Leads at 7.3% p.a.
medium.summary: A survey of online deposit rate boards as of June 27 shows ACB reclaiming the top spot for 12-month term deposits at 7.3% p.a., followed by Saigonbank at 7.2% p.a. and a cluster of banks (MBV, PGBank, VCBNeo, VIB) offering 7.0% p.a. for the same tenor. The four major state-owned banks — Agribank, BIDV, Vietcombank, and VietinBank — continue to maintain stable, lower deposit rate schedules. The persistence of private bank rates in the 6.9%–7.3% range for 12-month tenors signals ongoing competition for retail deposits, which could provide a floor for short-term government bond yields. Bond investors should note the spread between private bank deposit rates and sovereign yields as a key indicator of relative value; if credit growth accelerates following SBV's regulatory easing (see above), deposit rate pressure may intensify in Q3 2026.

medium.title: KienlongBank to Finalize Shareholder Register for ~30% Stock Dividend Next Week
medium.summary: KienlongBank (KLB) will close its shareholder register on July 3, 2026, for a stock dividend at a ratio of 29.5% — among the highest in the listed banking sector this year. The bank plans to issue over 170 million new shares, increasing charter capital from VND 5,822 billion to over VND 7,537 billion, a move previously approved by the SBV. While this is primarily a capital structure event rather than a macroeconomic signal, the SBV's approval underscores the regulator's broader push to strengthen bank capital buffers ahead of accelerated credit expansion. Investors tracking banking sector equity flows and capital adequacy ratios should note this as consistent with the sector-wide recapitalization trend in 2026.

medium.title: Vietnam Shrimp Exports Near $2 Billion USD: US and China Competing to Source, Vietnam Holds World-Leading Technology
medium.summary:
Vietnam's shrimp exports reached **$1.9 billion USD in the first five months of 2026**, up **12% year-on-year**, according to the Vietnam Association of Seafood Exporters and Processors (VASEP). China & Hong Kong emerged as the dominant growth engine, absorbing over **$711 million USD (+46% YoY)**, accounting for nearly 38% of total shrimp export value — driven by strong demand for frozen shrimp and lobster products. The US market, historically Vietnam's top destination, remains a drag, with exports declining 2% to $228 million USD. While this article is primarily a trade/commodity story, the strong export performance is modestly relevant to FX market participants as sustained hard currency inflows from seafood exports support the **current account balance** and provide a natural source of **USD supply** into the domestic FX market. For VND traders, continued export momentum at this pace could partially offset capital outflow pressures and reduce SBV intervention requirements in the second half of 2026.
